#!/bin/bash
#flux: --job-name=chroma-run
#flux: --nodes=1
#flux: --ntasks=1
#flux: --cpus-per-task=16
#flux: --mem-per-node=64G
#flux: --gpus-per-node=1
#flux: --output=chroma-run-%J.out
#flux: --error=chroma-run-%J.err
# The Slurm output filename format '%x-%N-%j' (jobname-nodename-jobid) is not fully supported in Flux.
# It has been simplified to 'jobname-%J.out', omitting the nodename. A job name has been added for clarity.

source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh

# WARNING: The following logic for module paths is based on the Slurm partition name
# and will not work in Flux. Flux does not have a direct equivalent for $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION.
# This logic needs to be adapted. One common approach is to use node features/constraints.
# For example, if nodes in a partition have a 'rhel8' feature, you could check for that.
# Since this is highly site-specific, the original logic is commented out.

# if [[ $(flux resource list -o '{nodelist}' | grep 'rhel8') ]]; then
#     module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
#     ...
# fi

module purge
module load rocm-5.4.3

tmp=/tmp/$USER/tmp-$$
mkdir -p $tmp

# Copy the benchmark data to avoid using --writable-tmpfs
singularity run /shared/apps/bin/chroma_3.43.0_29.sif cp -r /benchmark $tmp
singularity run --bind $tmp/benchmark:/benchmark --pwd /benchmark /shared/apps/bin/chroma_3.43.0_29.sif run-benchmark --ngpus 1

# Cleanup the benchmark data which was copied
rm -rf $tmp

issues: The job requests 16 CPUs for a single task (`--cpus-per-task=16`), but the application inside the container, `run-benchmark`, is only instructed to use a single GPU (`--ngpus 1`). It's unclear if the benchmark is multi-threaded and can utilize all 16 cores. If it is single-threaded, 15 of the 16 allocated CPU cores will be idle, leading to significant resource waste.

The script's core logic for setting up the correct module environment based on the OS has been commented out because it depends on a Slurm-specific variable. The script will fail if the default module path does not contain the required `rocm-5.4.3` module. This logic must be adapted to the target Flux system (e.g., using `flux resource list` to inspect node features) for the script to be portable and reliable.

#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=16
#SBATCH --mem=64GB
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH -o %x-%N-%j.out
#SBATCH -e %x-%N-%j.err

source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh

# Use partition name to load OS-specific modulespath to use to override
# login node environment
if [[ $(echo $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION | grep -i ubuntu) = *Ubuntu* ]]; then
    module use /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION | grep -i rhel8) = *RHEL8* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION | grep -i rhel9) = *RHEL9* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION | grep -i sles15) = *SLES15* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION | grep -i centos8) = *CentOS8* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION | grep -i rocky9) = *Rocky9* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
fi


module purge
module load rocm-5.4.3
tmp=/tmp/$USER/tmp-$$
mkdir -p $tmp

# Copy the benchmark data to avoid using --writable-tmpfs
singularity run /shared/apps/bin/chroma_3.43.0_29.sif cp -r /benchmark $tmp
